items.summary: “मुझे खुशी तभी होगी जब मेरी बेटी को इंसाफ मिलेगा. मैं चाहता हूं कि पुलिस उन्हें एनकाउंटर में मार दे. सिर्फ गिरफ्तारी काफी नहीं है.” ये दीपक कुमार की वो तमन्ना है जो गुस्से में लिपटी है, जिसमें उनकी बेटी के लिए न्याय की गुहार है. दरअसल, दसवीं कक्षा में पढ़ने वाली उनकी बेटी के साथ 19 सितंबर को बिहार के जमुई जिले में कुछ युवकों ने कथित तौर पर छेड़छाड़ और मारपीट की. मामले के एक मुख्य आरोपी नंदन यादव को 22 सितंबर को पुलिस ने पैर में गोली मारकर गिरफ्तार कर लिया. इसके साथ ही मामले में गिरफ्तार आरोपियों की संख्या छह हो गई है. द टाइम्स ऑफ इंडिया की रिपोर्ट मुताबिक, गिरफ्तार आरोपियों में तीन बालिग और तीन नाबालिग हैं. गौरतलब है कि घटना के वीडियो सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल होने के बाद मामला सामने आया. वीडियो में लड़की और उसके एक पुरुष मित्र को करीब एक घंटे तक कुछ लोगों से घिरा, पीछा और परेशान किया जाता हुआ देखा जा सकता है. वीडियो वायरल होने के बाद पुलिस ने मामले का संज्ञान लिया और जांच शुरू की. जमुई लोकसभा क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत तारापुर विधानसभा सीट आती है, जिसका प्रतिनिधित्व बिहार के मुख्यमंत्री सम्राट चौधरी करते हैं. घटना को लेकर विपक्षी नेताओं ने इलाके की कानून-व्यवस्था पर सवाल उठाए हैं. जमुई पुलिस ने यह भी बताया है कि उसने ऐसे 120 यूआरएल की पहचान की है, जहां घटना का वीडियो मौजूद है. पुलिस का कहना है कि वीडियो के प्रसार को रोकने के लिए कार्रवाई की जा रही है. 19 सितंबर को क्या हुआ? जानकारी के मुताबिक, 19 सितंबर की शाम करीब पांच बजे दसवीं कक्षा की छात्रा ट्यूशन पढ़ने के लिए घर से निकली थी. उसे उम्मीद थी कि शाम की पढ़ाई के बाद वह घर लौट आएगी. हालांकि, छात्रा के पिता की मानें तो ट्यूशन के दौरान ब्रेक में वह अपने एक पुरुष मित्र के साथ आइसक्रीम खाने बाहर गई थी. इसी दौरान दो बाइक पर सवार कुछ युवकों ने कथित तौर पर उसे परेशान करना और उसके साथ अभद्र व्यवहार करना शुरू कर दिया. दीपक कुमार ने न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री को बताया, “इस घटना के बाद मेरी बेटी काफी परेशान है. घटना के अगले दिन उसने हमें इसके बारे में बताया, जब वीडियो इंटरनेट पर वायरल होने लगा.” कथित तौर पर दोनों छात्रों को युवकों के समूह ने रोक लिया और करीब एक घंटे तक घेरकर परेशान किया. दोनों वहां से निकलने की कोशिश करते रहे. आरोप है कि नंदन यादव ने लड़की का पीछा किया, उसे पीछे से पकड़ लिया और बाद में अपनी गोद में उठा लिया. उसके पुरुष मित्र ने बीच में आकर लड़की को छुड़ाया, जिसके बाद दोनों पक्षों के बीच हाथापाई हुई. इसके बावजूद आरोपी दोनों को वहां से जाने से रोकने की कोशिश करते रहे. घटना के वीडियो सोशल मीडिया पर सामने आने के बाद जमुई पुलिस ने मामले का संज्ञान लिया और जांच शुरू की. जमुई के पुलिस अधीक्षक विश्वजीत दयाल के मुताबिक, 25 वर्षीय नंदन यादव फिलहाल पुलिस हिरासत में है और उससे पूछताछ के बाद मामले में और लोगों की पहचान हो सकती है. दयाल

items.title: Festivals not meant for people to die: Bombay High Court moots decibel caps, ban firecrackers on streets
items.summary: Celebrations during festivities are not meant for people to die or suffer, the Bombay High Court orally remarked on Tuesday. A division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale indicated that it will issue an order banning the bursting of firecrackers on public roads across Maharashtra during festivals like Ganeshotsav. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale The sharp remarks came during the hearing of a suo motu case initiated by the Court to address unchecked noise and air pollution caused by high-decibel amplifiers, loud music systems and firecrackers on public streets during festivals. The Court ordered authorities to take immediate preventive action instead of acting on delayed complaints. It directed police to measure noise levels on-site using decibel meters and confiscate equipment violating prescribed norms. “Celebrations are not meant for people to die or suffer health-wise. Nobody would accept this idea that celebrations are there, but at the cost of someone’s health,” the Court said. It also emphasised that celebrations could not happen at the cost of violation of the norms, rules and the tremendous inconvenience to the other citizens . “The excesses have to be controlled,” the judge said. Data submitted during the hearing recorded noise levels reaching up to 106 decibels. While the law permits extended hours until midnight on 15 designated festival days, strict daytime limits up to a maximum of 75 decibels remain mandatory. Advocates noted that those celebrating festivals bypass DJ bans by stacking speakers on pushcarts or beating heavy metal cylinders with hammers. The court criticised the current enforcement mechanism which involves police issuing minor fines of ₹5,000 that effectively act as blanket permissions to break the law. Justice Kulkarni remarked that action must be preventive, failing which damage to thousands of citizens would be already done. “ There is no point. First violating, then going and paying a fine is no good. Filing a criminal complaint, nothing will happen. It has to be preventive. Otherwise, the damage is already done. There is no point in having this kind of mechanism. That is not the correct law and order situation, ” the judge emphasised. The bench questioned why Maharashtra lacks a uniform policy when cities like Nagpur have proactively banned DJ sound systems and laser lights. items.title: Eight years and nine benches later, Delhi High Court begins hearing Mastercard tax dispute afresh
items.summary: Nearly eight years after Mastercard Asia Pacific approached the Delhi High Court, a Division Bench on Tuesday began hearing afresh its challenge to a tax ruling which held that the Singapore-based company had a permanent establishment in India [Mastercard Asia Pacific Vs Union of India] While acknowledging the prolonged history of the case, a Bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Aditi Choudhary indicated that it would like to render a decision in the case. “ We were told on the last occasion that it was heard and then released, so let us decide, ” the Bench remarked. When Senior Advocate Harish Salve , appearing for Mastercard, referred to the arguments made by him previously, the Bench pointed out that it was considering the dispute for the first time. “ We just want to remind you that we are, for the first time, hearing this case, ” it said. Senior Advocate Harish Salve Since the petition was filed in 2018, it has been listed before various benches led by Justices S Ravindra Bhat, S Muralidhar, Vipin Sanghi, Manmohan, Rajiv Shakdher, Yashwant Varma, Prathiba M Singh, V Kameswar Rao and Dinesh Mehta . A majority of these judges have retired or are no longer posted at Delhi. Mastercard is challenging a 2018 ruling of the Authority for Advance Rulings (AAR), which held that the company has multiple permanent establishments in India and consequently, the sum received by it from its customer banks located in India is liable to tax in India. The dispute concerns whether Mastercard Interface Processors (MIPs) - installed at Indian banks, its telecommunications network and the activities of its Indian subsidiary, creates a taxable presence under the India-Singapore Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement. The AAR had held that the MIPs performed significant functions connected with the processing of card transactions and were not engaged merely in preparatory or auxiliary activities. It had also found that part of the fees received by Mastercard from Indian customers qualified as royalty. When the ruling was challenged before the High Court, the tax authorities were restrained from passing final assessment orders pursuant to the AAR ruling. In September 2021, the High Court continued that protection for assessment years 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2020-21, noting that Mastercard was depositing the applicable tax. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Tuesday acquitted a woman who was sentenced to death by a trial court last year in connection with the murder of her three minor children in June 2024 [Priyanka v State pf UP and Another] The accused Priyanka had been convicted along with her cousin-in-law Ashish alias Daini, who was sentenced to life imprisonment for conspiracy in the murder case. A Division Bench of Justice Siddhartha Varma and Justice Jai Krishna Upadhyay acquitted the accused of their charges after finding that the prosecution miserably failed to establish their guilt beyond reasonable doubt. "The conviction recorded by the learned trial court rests on statement of an uncorroborated, tutored, and contradictory child witness, coupled with a fatal failure to produce the best available evidence, unreliable deposition of PW-1 and investigative lapses. Therefore, the Court is inclined to grant benefit of doubt to the accused appellants on the ground of rule of caution," the Court said. Justice Siddhartha Varma and Justice Jai Krishan Upadhyay On June 27 in 2024, 6-year-old Madhav @ Gunga, 5-year-old Aditya @ Tilla and 4-year-old Mangal were found dead near a bridge of Sengur river. A complaint lodged by their uncle Manish alleged that the accused Priyanka along with Ashish alias Daini, a cousin brother of her deceased husband, had taken her four sons to the bridge and tried to kill them all. However, Sonu, one of the children, had managed to escape the attempt of his mother, the police was told. The complainant further said that Priyanka, whose husband had died two years prior to the incident, was in love with Ashish and wanted to get rid of the children to continue their relationship. It was mainly the child's testimony that had led to the conviction of the accused, including his mother. items.title: Only case where ED proceeded on private complaint: Sonia and Rahul Gandhi to Delhi High Court on National Herald case
items.summary: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi have told the Delhi High Court that the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) National Herald money laundering case against them is a result of “extraneous” considerations. They have argued that this was the only case in the country where the ED had proceeded based on a private complaint. According to Gandhis' reply, the ED registered the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) against them based on a private complaint filed by former Union Minister Subramanian Swamy, but the same is not permitted under the law. This shows that the National Herald case was being singled out by the ED, contrary to the agency's own interpretation of law, they claimed. The Congress leaders have stated that the ED itself had consistently taken the position that a money laundering investigation could not be initiated in the absence of an FIR in the scheduled or predicate offence. According to the replies, the ED did not register an ECIR on a complaint filed by Subramanian Swamy in 2014 and only registered the ECIR on June 30, 2021, about 7 years later. The Gandhis have relied on this delay to contend that the agency’s conduct was consistent with its understanding that a private complaint could not, by itself, trigger proceedings under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). “The calculated silence of the department [ED] before the Ld Trial Court during the course of arguments and even before this Hon’ble Court in the revision petition, as to why the present case is being singled out by the department to take a different stand, contrary to law and international standards laid down by FATF, speaks volumes about the extraneous considerations surrounding the case,” the replies state. The National Herald case stems from a private complaint by Swamy accusing Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Motilal Vora, Oscar Fernandes, Suman Dubey, Sam Pitroda, and Gandhi family-controlled Young Indian of cheating, criminal conspiracy, criminal breach of trust and misappropriation of property. The ED filed a prosecution complaint against the Gandhis as well as Pitroda and others on April 15, 2025. However, the trial court passed an order on December 16, 2025, refusing to take cognisance of the matter. The Court ruled that since the case was based on a private complaint filed by Swamy before a magistrate and not any First Information Report (FIR), it was not maintainable. items.title: Kerala consumer court orders lift company to refund ₹2.69 lakh to retired High Court judge, wife
items.summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) at Ernakulam recently directed Nibav Lifts to refund ₹2.69 lakh with interest to a retired Kerala High Court judge and his wife after finding deficiency in services and unfair trade practice in connection with the proposed installation of a home elevator [Justice (Retd) TR Ramachandran Nair & anr v Nibav Lifts Private Ltd & anr]. A Bench of President DB Binu along with members V Ramachandran and Sreevidhia TN found that the company had failed to properly analyse whether the lift could be installed at the couple's residence before accepting the advance payment. The commission stressed that consumers cannot be expected to have the technical knowledge required to understand the consequences of installing such equipment and added that the responsibility was on the company, which had the necessary technical expertise to properly examine the site and explain the implications of the installation. " From the foregoing discussion, it is evident that the opposite parties had not exercised proper attention; care etc. while entering into the agreement of installation of the lift at the house of the complainants or they ought not have made proper and adequate assessment of the feasibility of installing the lift in the house of the complainant. The complainants need not be technically skill enough to evaluate the consequences of installing the machine even before it is being installed, " the commission said on August 13. It thus ordered Nibav Lifts and its Business Development Manager to jointly refund ₹2,69,865 to the couple along with an interest of 7.25% from the date of filing of the complaint until the payment. The commission also ordered the company to pay ₹25,000 towards litigation costs. Retired Justice TR Ramachandran Nair and his wife had approached Nibav Lifts after coming across an advertisement for its home elevators on YouTube. The couple wanted a lift since their bedroom was not on the ground floor and the judge's wife had been medically advised to avoid climbing stairs. A company representative inspected their house and identified certain portions as suitable locations for installing the lift. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday took serious exception to the absence of price-control mechanisms for life-saving medicines as it flagged huge differences between the Price to Retailer (PTR) and Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of cancer-curing drugs [ Kishan Chand Jain v. Union of India ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the difference in prices is nothing short of daylight robbery being committed on vulnerable patients by drug manufacturers and retailers. "There are essential medicines for cancer for which MRP is ₹27,000 and PTR is ₹2,700. That is absolute rampage and carnage and broad daylight dacoity with the patients. How can a patient be cheated for a medicine which the manufacturer sells to the retailer at ₹2,700 and MRP is printed at ₹27,000? It is surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take a decision on this are absolutely silent. We need not spell out the reasons for that," Justice Mehta remarked. The Court further noted that such inflated pricing structures result in systemic fraud on public exchequers when medical expenses are reimbursed under state health schemes. "When patients are taking treatment under Ayushman Bharat scheme, this whole price has to be paid by the taxpayers. Hospitals are buying medicines at these prices and then reimbursing from the government. It’s ultimately taxpayer’s money. There is a clear-cut case of fraud," the Court added. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The Court was hearing a petition seeking mandatory generic drug prescriptions, strict initial price controls on non-scheduled medicines, and maximum retail price caps on medical devices. During the hearing, petitioner Kishan Chand Jain submitted that under the Drug Price Control Order (DPCO) of 2013, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) fixes ceiling prices for only around 1,000 "scheduled" drugs, leaving nearly 82 per cent of medicines in the market non-scheduled. items.title: Spoiling his own case: Bombay High Court pulls up Vijay Mallya for posting ED affidavit on X
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday orally reprimanded fugitive businessman Vijay Mallya for uploading an Enforcement Directorate (ED) affidavit onto X, noting that such postings undermine the efficacy of the court. [Vijay Vittal Mallya v. State Bank of India & Ors] Justice Milind Jadhav cautioned Mallya’s legal team that fighting legal battles on social media harms their own case. "Please make your client understand, this is not the way to do it. What happens is, it undermines the efficacy of the court then,” the judge remarked during the hearing. Justice Milind Jadhav The objection was raised by ED counsel, who informed the Bench that after emailing the affidavit to Mallya’s legal team at 4:30 PM, Mallya uploaded the entire document on X by 11 PM that same night accompanied by derogatory remarks. “This is not fair to Your Lordship's court...Your Lordship has not even had the chance to see it. The applicant should fight it out in court, not on Twitter,” the ED counsel submitted. The judge also added, “The problem is, he's spoiling his own case. If he's doing like this. You have very competent lawyers in the court, argue the matter." Appearing for Mallya, Senior Advocate Amit Desai assured the Court that they would convey the message to their client. He also pointed out how the ED also routinely posted about Mallya. The core dispute centers on Mallya’s application regarding asset recoveries by central agencies. In its affidavit, ED revealed that it handed over approximately ₹14,131 crore to the State Bank of India (SBI)-led consortium through the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT). Desai argued that this recovery far exceeds the original decreed debt of roughly ₹6,600 crore plus interest. Justice Jadhav directed the SBI consortium to file a fresh affidavit addressing the ED's disclosures, after which Mallya was permitted to file a comprehensive amendment application. The matter has been listed for further hearing on October 13. items.title: P&H High Court raps Punjab for delay tactics in employees' DA case, summons Chief Secretary

items.title: Supreme Court refuses to entertain plea alleging misuse of SC/ST Act
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to entertain a plea challenging the 2018 amendment to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 which restored the bar on anticipatory bail and removed the requirement of a preliminary inquiry before registration of a first information report (FIR) under the Act. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana did not agree with the petitioner's contention that the Act was leading to reverse discrimination against people belonging to other castes. The Court observed that sufficient safeguards already exist under the law including the power of the courts to examine whether a prima facie case under the Act is made out or not. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The petitioner also questioned the payment of compensation to the victims under the SC/ST Act. The counsel representing the petitioner told the Court that ₹493 crore had been distributed as compensation to the victims and argued that the scheme was literally "inviting people to lodge FIRs". However, the Court was not convinced by the submissions and refused to hear the plea. The plea challenged the 2018 amendment to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, which introduced Section 18A. The amendment followed the Supreme Court's 2018 ruling in Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v State of Maharashtra . That judgment had introduced safeguards relating to preliminary inquiry and arrest, and held that there was no absolute bar on anticipatory bail under the Act. The parliament subsequently amended the law to undo the effect of those directions. The amendment was upheld by a three-judge Bench of the Supreme Court in Prathvi Raj Chauhan v Union of India in 2020. The petitioner argued that the amendment could not nullify the earlier judgment without curing the defects identified by the Court in its 2018 ruling. The Bench, however, noted that the amendment had already been upheld and declined to reopen the issue. items.title: Private universities cannot be run for profit: Supreme Court orders disclosure of finances, fees et al.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Central government, States and Union Territories (UTs) to collect detailed information about the finances, admissions, fees, use of surplus funds, staff recruitment and grievance-redressal systems of private universities and colleges. [Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida and Others] In an order passed on 17 September, a Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and NV Anjaria issued the directions while making it clear that private universities could not be run as commercial ventures. “ No private university shall be allowed to be run as a profit-making institution. It has to serve a purpose with some sort of a cushion so that its finances/resources are responsibly managed to ensure smooth functioning of the institution and that the teaching and non-teaching employees are compensated suitably, ” the Court said. The Bench added that funds beyond this requirement could not be diverted towards purposes such as paying members of governing boards or providing facilities to them. Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and NV Anjaria The case originated from a petition filed by one Ayesha Jain against Amity University at Noida over the university’s handling of the change of her name in its records and the academic consequences allegedly suffered by her. However, as the case progressed, the Court expanded its scope to examine wider issues concerning the establishment, regulation and functioning of private universities across the country. Supreme Court No private university shall be allowed to be run as a profit-making institution. In its latest order passed on September 17, the Court directed the States to ensure that private universities under their jurisdiction submit their audited accounts for the past five years. The Court said the records must show how the universities generated and utilised their funds and provide details of payments made to people who were not directly connected with their functioning as educational institutions. items.title: Investigating officer can prosecute case before Navy court-martial: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday held that an officer who investigates a case against Navy personnel can also be appointed to prosecute the same case before a court-martial, since the Navy Regulations do not prohibit such an arrangement [ Union of India & ors v Santosh Karwade & anr ]. A Division Bench of Justice K Natarajan and Justice Johnson John held that such an appointment of the investigating officer as a prosecutor would not, by itself, violate the right to a fair trial under Article 21 of the Constitution. " On a thorough reading of the Regulations, there is no prohibition on an Investigating Officer from being appointed as a Prosecutor. The Investigating Officer may be a suitable person for conducting the prosecution case before the court-martial, who knows the facts of the case and who finally files the charge sheet against the Armed personnel, " the Court added. Justice K Natarajan and Justice Johnson John The ruling came in appeals filed by the Union government an a naval officer named Santosh Karwade against a 2025 judgment of a single judge Bench of the High Court. Karwade, who had served in the Navy for 31 years, was facing a court-martial under the Navy Act, 1957. Among other allegations, he was accused of dishonestly persuading an officer to transfer ₹1.10 lakh. He approached the Court alleging that he had been denied a free and fair trial, as the officer who investigated the allegations against him was subsequently appointed as a prosecutor in the same court-martial proceedings. Karwade challenged Regulation 178(3) of the Navy (Discipline and Miscellaneous Provisions) Regulations, 1965 (Regulations), which permits a prosecutor to be a competent witness. He argued that allowing the investigating officer to perform the roles of both a prosecutor and an investigating officer under this provision was contrary to basic principles of criminal law and violated of Article 21. A single judge Bench of the Court refused to declare Regulation 178(3) of the Regulations as unconstitutional. The single-judge's ruling was challenged on this aspect by Karwade in his appeal. Notably, the single-judge Bench also clarified that the expression ' suitable person ' in Regulation 163(1) (governing appointment of prosecutors) could not be interpreted to allow the appointment of an investigating officer as prosecutor who had investigated the same case, as it would infringe the right to a fair trial. items.title: Supreme Court moots common platform to invest money deposited by litigants in courts
items.summary: The Supreme Court has proposed the creation of a common platform to pool and invest money deposited before different courts and tribunals by litigants [National Seeds Vs National Agro Seeds]. In a judgment delivered on September 17, a bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe observed that the present system lacks uniformity and can lead to financial loss for litigants Hence, the bench opined that deposits made before different courts and tribunals could be brought under a unified scheme and invested in financial instruments that are most beneficial to the parties. “ This common platform will not only create certainty in the interest rates and increase the ease of accessibility for litigants but will also ease the burden on Courts/Tribunals regarding how this money deposited is to be invested and dealt with ,” the Court said. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The Court made the observations while deciding a dispute between National Seeds Corporation Limited and National Agro Seed Corporation (India) concerning interest payable on money deposited during a challenge to an arbitral award. The Bench noted that there is presently no statutory prescription or uniform rule governing how decretal amounts deposited before courts or tribunals should be handled. Instead, courts and tribunals have been passing orders on a case-to-case basis, resulting in “a great amount of disparity and inconsistency”, the judgment said. The Court identified several areas where this lack of uniformity causes problems, including the percentage of a decretal amount required to be deposited for obtaining a stay, the bank or financial institution in which the money is to be kept, the financial instrument used, the applicable rate of interest and the manner in which such interest is ultimately adjusted. It added that decree-holders may be prevented from using money already awarded to them, while judgment-debtors may continue facing mounting interest liability even after parting with the money. The absence of common standards can also result in similarly placed litigants receiving different treatment depending on the court or tribunal before which their proceedings are pending, the Court noted. It further said that uncertainty over the administration of deposits and interest can generate fresh litigation even after the underlying dispute has ended. items.title: Fountain Court's Alex Taylor on choosing a 47-year career in clerking over joining Fulham FC at age 16
items.summary: In July 1979, a 16-year-old Alex Taylor had a decision to make: take up a football apprenticeship at Fulham FC or join Fountain Court Chambers as a junior clerk, the lowest-paid and least familiar option on the table. He picked clerking. After 47 years, one senior clerkship and a chambers that grew from roughly 20 members to 116, Taylor is preparing to hand over the reins to Sian Huckett, who takes over as senior clerk in January 2027. In conversation with Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja , Taylor traces the evolution of clerking, from a paper-and-diary era with no formal career path to a sophisticated practice built on business development and client relationships. He also speaks on Fountain Court's deepening ties with India and a growing pipeline of Indian instructions into both London and Singapore. [Watch Interview] Edited excerpts follow. Pallavi Saluja (PS): Can you tell us how you got into clerking and the fact that you started at the age of 16? Alex Taylor (AT): It was through a careers officer at school. I was in a fortunate position, I'd been offered several jobs. Clerking was the least paid and the least familiar to my family. It really came down to a toss-up: take the clerkship, or take up an apprenticeship playing football at Fulham, who weren't in the Premier League at the time but were in the First Division. I made a very mature decision, in my opinion, and accepted an offer at Fountain Court Chambers. I started as a junior clerk in July 1979. PS: Can you explain what clerking actually is, for readers who may not be familiar with barristers' chambers in the UK? AT: I've seen a lot of changes in the 47 years I've been doing this. items.title: Karnataka High Court nominates two women advocates as co-opted members of State Bar Council
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has nominated Senior Advocate S Susheela and Advocate Vijayamma V as co-opted members of the Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC). The nominations were made by Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru , after consultation with the elected members of the State Bar Council. A communication issued by High Court Registrar General M. Chandrashekar Reddy on September 10 confirmed the nominations. The move follows the Supreme Court's August 4 directions in Yogamaya MG v. Union of India and connected proceedings, under which Chief Justices of High Courts were empowered to nominate two women advocates as members of their respective State Bar Councils. The Supreme Court's directions were issued in the backdrop of concerns over inadequate representation of women in elected bodies governing the legal profession. The mechanism provides for the co-option of women members in consultation with elected members of the respective State Bar Councils. Meanwhile, elections for the posts of KSBC Chairman and Vice Chairman are scheduled to be held on October 1. September 22 is the last date for filing nominations. As of Tuesday, elected members and Advocates N Devaraj and Rajanna have filed their nominations for the post of Chairman. Advocates Shivamurthy and Shylaja K has filed nominations for the post of Vice-Chairman. Advocates CM Dhananjaya and Shiva Kumar N has filed his nominations for the Bar Council of India nominee post from the Karnataka State Bar Council. The Advocate General of Karnataka, 2 co-opted women members and 23 elected members of the Karnataka State Bar Council will constitute the electoral body for choosing the Chairman, Vice-Chairman and Bar Council of India (BCI) nominee. items.summary: Former Mylapore MLA and DMK leader Dha Velu has moved the Madras High Court challenging the Tamil Nadu government's decision to construct a new Legislative Assembly and Secretariat complex at Foreshore Estate in Chennai's Pattinapakkam. Velu has sought quashing of a September 8 Government Order granting in-principle approval for the proposed complex. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia Bus drivers, conductors and other personnel associated with the operation of public buses, have been on strike since September 15 to demand an increase in their wages and other benefits. The PIL is seeking directions for urgent restoration, maintenance and continuity of public bus transport services in Delhi. Stalin said that while he exercises administrative control over office bearers of the party’s various wings, this cannot translate into legal liability for their individual acts. Arjuna has maintained that the accused John Britto is not his relative. He accused the DMK of deliberately conflating the drug accused with Arjuna's relative, because they shared similar names. The DMK's post linking Arjuna and Britto was subsequently deleted. Arjuna then moved the High Court against Stalin and the DMK IT Wing, seeking ₹1 crore in damages, an apology and injunctive relief. items.title: Justice RC Chavan resigns from Maharashtra Uniform Civil Code panel; flags concerns over its functioning
items.summary: Former Bombay High Court Justice RC Chavan has resigned from Maharashtra’s Uniform Civil Code (UCC) drafting committee, raising serious concerns over the panel's functioning, the rushed finalization of a public feedback questionnaire, and the active participation of an un-appointed non-member. The seven-member committee, chaired by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Desai , recently held its second meeting online. In a candid resignation email addressed to the Chairperson, members, and the Principal Secretary (Law and Judiciary), Justice Chavan revealed that crucial decision-making processes were being bypassed. Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai Justice Chavan noted that during the meeting, three members attempted to articulate their views including a suggestion to have the questionnaire professionally evaluated by academic experts. However, those inputs were rendered moot as the chairperson had already finalised the document. "The Honourable chairperson had already circulated a questionnaire finalized by her and stated that it would be uploaded once the website was ready," Justice Chavan wrote. The former judge expressed deep disappointment with the committee's reduced scope for gathering public input. "My attempt to put forth my views... was due to my misunderstanding that our exercise was aimed at gathering views of people of Maharashtra and to generate a consensus to remedy the issues of late marriages, perversions, infertility, unstable marriages, time consuming dispute resolution mechanism etc.,” the judge said. He realised that the aim now remained to gather the ‘yes or no’ responses so that analysis of data becomes easy. Justice Chavan also questioned the involvement and directives of an outsider, former IAS officer Shatrughna Singh, regarding the committee's website modifications. He speculated whether this reliance on an external figure stemmed from an apprehension among state officials regarding their own competence. "To solve this problem, I am vacating my seat on the committee by resigning now, so that the Government can fill in the blank promptly. A resolution notified quickly will help me tell those who meet me with the expectation that I will place their views before the committee that they must do it themselves. This will also relieve me from the injunction to avoid interactions. Now as a free citizen, I will be free to air my views," the judge said. The Maharashtra government has accepted his resignation. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana asked the government to respond to Carnatic vocalist TM Krishna's petition within two weeks. Pertinently, Justice Bagchi remarked during the hearing that the Supreme Court's earlier ruling in the Bijoe Emmanuel case protecting those who choose not to sing the national anthem continues to hold the field. Hence, a conscientious objector who does not recite one or all stanzas of Vande Mataram should not face criminal prosecution, the judge said. "We would expect that the law of the land, as declared by this Court in Bijoe Emmanuel, will govern the act of the statute. The declaration of law in Bijoe Emmanuel has till now not been questioned," the judge said. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Krishna moved the Court questioning Section 3 of the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 (the law protecting national symbols), as amended in 2026. items.title: Can civil courts hear trademark suits? Supreme Court refers issue to larger bench
items.summary: A larger bench of the Supreme Court will decide whether trademark infringement suits can be heard by commercial courts below the level of a district court despite the Trade Marks Act expressly barring such suits before courts inferior to a district court [ISDS Vs Khemka]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there appeared to be a conflict between earlier Supreme Court rulings on how special statutes such as the Trade Marks Act and Arbitration Act interact with the Commercial Courts Act. “ In our humble view the legislative imprimatur cannot be diluted by the notifications issued by the High Courts, ” the Court said. The Court consequently directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India for constitution of an appropriate larger Bench so that the law could be settled uniformly across States. The issue arose in an appeal filed by ISDS Private Limited against Khemka Food Products Private Limited. Section 134 of the Trade Marks Act provides that suits relating to trademark infringement and certain other reliefs cannot be instituted before a court inferior to a district court. However, under the Commercial Courts Act, High Courts in some States have notified civil judges (senior division) as commercial courts. In Jharkhand, such courts have been given jurisdiction over commercial disputes valued between ₹3 lakh and ₹1 crore. The appellants argued that allowing trademark suits to be instituted before civil judges (Senior Division) would dilute the specific mandate of the Trade Marks Act. They also pointed out that an appeal from such a commercial court would lie to the district court rather than the High Court. Consequently, a litigant would not have a regular appellate remedy before the High Court and would largely be confined to revisional or supervisory jurisdiction. The respondents argued that intellectual property disputes are expressly recognised as commercial disputes under the Commercial Courts Act. They contended that the Commercial Courts Act was a later special legislation intended to ensure speedy adjudication of commercial disputes and that its overriding provision would prevail over inconsistent provisions in earlier laws. items.title: Police officer who fails to furnish written grounds of arrest must face departmental inquiry: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that when police seek to re-arrest an accused released due to their failure to furnish written grounds of arrest, the investigation must be transferred to another officer and a departmental inquiry initiated against the officers responsible for failing to furnish the grounds of arrest [ Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v. State of Punjab ]. A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar reiterated that a failure to furnish written grounds of arrest violates Article 22(1) of the Constitution and renders the arrest illegal. Consequently, any accused arrested without such grounds being furnished must be released from illegal and unconstitutional detention, the Court held. The Bench clarified that such a release does not permanently protect the accused from arrest in the same case. However, if the investigating agency still requires the accused’s custody, it must first furnish the written grounds of arrest and obtain permission from the concerned magistrate. The Bench added that the custody application must explain why the grounds were not supplied at the time of the initial arrest and why custodial interrogation is necessary. “ Once there is a breach of Article 22(1) of the Constitution, the power to re-arrest the accused must not be left to the discretion of the very same authority who had violated the said provision of the Constitution. It must have the judicial imprimatur, ” the Court further said. The magistrate may permit re-arrest only after being satisfied that the grounds could not initially be supplied for bona fide reasons, that they were furnished after the accused’s release and that re-arrest is necessary, the Court held. While reaffirming the procedure laid down in Mihir Rajesh Shah v. State of Maharashtra , the Court introduced additional safeguards governing any attempt to secure the accused’s custody again. The Bench directed that the custody application must carry the endorsement of the investigating officer’s immediate superior. The superior officer must then transfer the investigation to another officer and order a departmental inquiry into the lapse, the Court added. “ On the administrative side, the superior authority when presented with the application seeking his endorsement for custody of the accused who has been released for violation of Article 22(1) shall hand over the investigation of the case to another officer, further directing departmental enquiry for such a serious lapse. items.summary: The Law and Society Committee (LawSoc) at National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru has decided not to proceed with the screening of Lalit Vachani's documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid , Prisoner No. 626710 is Present . In an email to students, LawSoc said that the planned screening had been met with serious threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment. "As LawSoc, we continue to be undeterred and committed deeply to questions of freedom and justice. Equally, we are committed to the safety and security of our own peers and the wider NLS community. Thus, after several rounds of discussions with the SBA and administration, we have decided not to proceed with the screening of the film, but to instead engage informatively and critically on the questions relating to criminal justice that the present moment raises," the email added. The email further stated that the decision was not a cancellation of Political Prisoners Day, nor was it a decision to step away from the conversation. The screening was originally scheduled for September 14, to mark Political Prisoners' Day (September 13) and 6 years since Khalid's arrest in a case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) had been campaigning for the screening's cancellation since it was first announced. It was then deferred to September 19 , citing logistical and security considerations around the Ganesh Chaturthi festival. At the time, LawSoc said that the move was not a response to pressure. According to sources, LawSoc and the NLSIU administration discussed the matter at length. Their assessment was that the screening was "not exactly in the white" on legality, and that a Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) social media post may have signalled scrutiny to come. items.title: No interim relief for Ravi Nair as Gujarat HC gives Adani time to reply
items.summary: Investigative journalist Ravi Nair, who is facing a probe by the Gujarat police in a complaint filed by an employee of Adani Group over a tweet he posted on ‘X’, has been lodged in judicial custody since September 17. The Gujarat High Court which heard the case again on Monday, September 21, has now given two-day’s time for Adani Group to file a response to Ravi’s plea challenging the arrest. The case came up for hearing at the bench of justice MK Thakkar of Gujarat High Court. Though Ravi’s counsel pleaded for interim relief, the court postponed the case for two days. The counsel representing the Adani Group requested more time to submit legal and factual points in the case. Advocate Abhik Chimni appearing for Ravi asked why his client should spend even one day in jail in a case that was at an appellate stage. However, the court observed that the complainant should be given fair opportunity for responding to the notice. Ravi was slapped with a non-bailable warrant after he failed to appear for a hearing in an appeal filed by him at the Gandhinagar court on September 3. Though Ravi approached the Sessions court to cancel the warrant, his application was rejected and he was sent to Sabarmati Central jail. On Tuesday, September 22, Amnesty international expressed concerns over the arrest of Ravi while his appeal is pending before the Gujarat High Court in a case of criminal defamation. “It poses serious questions around people's freedom of expression and fair trial rights in the country,” it said in a post on X. The non-bailable warrant was issued on September 3 without giving a formal summons or notice to Ravi. The Gandhinagar court has been hearing Ravi’s petition challenging his conviction and one-year imprisonment in the criminal defamation case. Ravi was convicted for a term of one year in the criminal defamation case by the Judicial Magistrate First Class court in Gandhinagar on February 2. The case was based on a complaint filed by an employee of the Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone limited (APSEZ) for a series of tweets he had posted on his ‘X’ account between October 2020 and July 2021. This conviction was suspended based on his appeal in March. According to Ravi’s counsel, an application for exemption from his personal appearance was rejected and a non-bailable warrant was issued on September 3, without any prior notice or without resorting to the immediate step of a bailable warrant.
